players.product: photonic fault-tolerant quantum computers; Inception photonic chip manufacturing facility (Toronto, 158,000 sq ft)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: Q2 2026 revenue was CAD 1.5 million, compared to CAD 2.8 million in Q1 2026 and CAD 1.1 million in the prior-year quarter, primarily driven by DARPA at Stage B.
quarterly_data.figure: CAD 1.5 million Q2 2026 revenue (vs CAD 2.8 million Q1 2026; CAD 1.1 million Q2 2025)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: R&D expense was approximately CAD 19.7 million, up CAD 2.4 million from Q1 2026 on headcount and stock-based compensation as manufacturing and engineering teams grow; G&A approximately CAD 11.1 million (vs CAD 9.8 million); adjusted EBITDA loss CAD 21.3 million (vs CAD 13.9 million in Q1 2026), driven by higher R&D and G&A and lower grant revenue. Cash at quarter end was CAD 312.8 million.
quarterly_data.figure: R&D ~CAD 19.7 million; adjusted EBITDA loss CAD 21.3 million; CAD 312.8 million cash

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: capex increased to approximately CAD 6.4 million in the quarter, mainly specialized equipment to test, refine and scale chip manufacturing. Xanadu gives no explicit guidance, but expects R&D growth to accelerate into Q3 and capex to increase further in the second half as it adds engineering talent and increases tapeouts — operating spend and capex should 'grow substantially in the second half of the year'; more color at its Analyst Day.

CEO: a new milestone in ultra-low-loss photonic chip packaging — an average edge coupling loss of 0.085 dB per facet — from its internal advanced photonic chip packaging facility (brought online last year), a close collaboration with Corning on customized fiber and fiber array solutions, and DISCO on wafer singulation. He calls the fiber-to-chip coupling 'world-class' and, 'we believe, the lowest loss anywhere in the world'; it is one of 16 or 17 major loss components being engineered down.
quarterly_data.figure: 0.085 dB per facet average edge coupling loss
quarterly_data.counterparty_role: collaborators (customized fiber and fiber arrays; wafer singulation)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: working with its foundry partners, Xanadu increased fabrication runs on thin-film lithium niobate by roughly 75% and on silicon nitride by roughly 50%. At NY Creates, which makes the silicon nitride primarily used for its qubits, wafers went from around 100 at the start of last quarter to 150; at WaferTech, from around 100 ('a bit more') to 175 wafers per month; NY Creates is 'likely to go up more' and WaferTech 'likely to go up in the next quarter as well'.
quarterly_data.figure: TFLN runs up roughly 75%; silicon nitride up roughly 50%; 150 wafers (NY Creates); 175 wafers per month (WaferTech)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: the optical loss gap has decreased up to 200x over the last four years ('I believe') and Xanadu is around 5 to 10x reduction away from where it needs to be ('the promised land'), still on track; a detailed loss roadmap and hardware milestone roadmap extrapolated to about 2030 is due at the end of summer (on track); the fault-tolerant target remains end of decade, 2029-2030. On DARPA Stage C: 'We're looking good for Stage C, we can't make any promises.'
quarterly_data.figure: up to 200x reduction over four years; 5 to 10x reduction left

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: in July Xanadu announced a significant expansion of its U.S. operations anchored in Albany, N.Y., giving direct access to established U.S. semiconductor and photonics supply chains; its U.S. workforce has grown more than fivefold since 2023 and is expected to grow significantly again by year-end. He says hiring has improved since going public and R&D engineer onboarding should accelerate further.
quarterly_data.figure: U.S. workforce up more than fivefold since 2023

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: Xanadu shipped PennyLane version 0.45 and Catalyst version 0.15; its QROM algorithm (patent filed, available in PennyLane) cuts the Toffoli gate operations needed by roughly half; it trained a quantum model with over one million parameters; the PennyLane white paper passed 2,000 citations. COO: PennyLane active users, universities and corporate users keep growing (exact numbers not reported).

CEO: Xanadu re-signed a multi-year collaboration with Rolls-Royce on quantum algorithms for computational fluid dynamics and aerodynamics; with Lockheed Martin (a long-time PennyLane user, per the COO) it launched a joint quantum machine learning initiative and a workforce-training effort giving engineers access to PennyLane, educational resources and workshops; it partnered with Oak Ridge National Laboratory to bring PennyLane onto the Frontier exascale supercomputer (distributed Lightning simulator support); and it continues a research collaboration with the Fidelity Center for Applied Technology and advanced-stage engagements with several major banks (not named) on quantum algorithms.
